I am 62 years old and have farmed this same 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and do my own counting, but honestly I learn most from doing and from watching my neighbors. Last year my wheat made about 530 jin per mu and my maize made about 590 jin per mu. This year I will do what worked last year because change is risky and a bad harvest is a disaster.

For my winter wheat: After the maize comes off in early June, I rotary till the ground and sow my wheat in October. I plant an improved variety, about 25 jin of seed per mu. For base fertilizer, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg per bag — and then at green-up time in March I topdress with half a bag of urea, 25 kg per mu. That gives me about 19 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 7.5 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I know fertilizer prices went up, but last year my neighbor Chen tried to save money by skipping urea and his wheat turned yellow and dropped yield. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose the crop. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray twice — herbicide in early spring and one insecticide spray if I see aphids.

For my summer maize: I use hybrid seed from the dealer, the same kind my neighbor Lao Zhang planted last year because he got over 600 jin per mu. Right after wheat harvest in June, I sow maize with no-tillage to save time — you cannot delay in summer because the heat comes fast. At planting I put one bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg, in the seed rows. When the plants are knee-high I spread 30 kg of urea per mu as topdressing. That is about 21 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I irrigate three times: once at seedling stage if rain is short, once at big trumpet in July, and once at grain filling. I spray twice — herbicide right after sowing and insecticide once in summer for corn borer.

My farm is only 6 mu, so every input is real money. It is just me and my husband working it. We hire nobody unless harvest is rushed. I watch the other families around me — most use similar amounts, so I stick close to that. Spending more on fertilizer means less left for other things, but going hungry next winter would be worse.
